historical_anchors: Historical TF58 departed Majuro on 6 Jun for FORAGER; historical Japanese C6N/MyRT reconnaissance on 9 Jun found the anchorage emptied and warned that TF58 was moving.
Historical TF58 began Marianas strikes on 11 Jun.

branch_progress.US: Lead TF58 groups depart Majuro. The 3 Jun Seiran strike produces loading/inspection friction but does not stop the sortie.
branch_progress.Japan: Communications/logistics pattern changes strengthen the existing CRITICAL Marianas warning but do not yet yield a fleet track.

branch_progress.US: Remaining/most delayed elements clear the Majuro support cycle and rejoin the movement plan; the small sortie stagger is operationally absorbed.
branch_progress.Japan: Submarine/air-recon sectors are weighted farther east/northeast; no weapon-quality contact.
Majuro silence plus picket/recon negatives makes a major westbound US carrier operation HIGH-confidence. Marianas becomes the dominant interpretation, but exact target and D-day remain unknown.

A high-speed long-range reconnaissance check confirms Majuro is largely emptied of the fast-carrier concentration. This closes the operational-warning question: TF58 is at sea and a Central Pacific major operation is imminent.

Warning is converted into preliminary A-GO deployment measures: submarines/pickets and base reconnaissance tighten, oilers/forward logistics prepare, fleet readiness rises. Main carrier force still does not sortie east without the strike/landing geometry.

US_branch_OOB_guard: Use current 8 CV + 8 CVL / 16 fast-deck branch pool before combat losses/detachments, not the legacy 7 CV + 8 CVL settlement.
sortie_friction_result: The Seiran raid causes hours-scale staggering only. By 10 Jun it no longer changes TF58 ability to execute an 11 Jun carrier strike.
guard: Do not pre-award the 11 Jun air battle or Japanese carrier release before the 11 Jun focused adjudication.
